record.headline: LegalZoom renamed its LLC plans and reshuffled them: the $249 plan now comes with a business advisor instead of attorney consultations, and the $299 plan adds a full team and tax filing with a higher renewal price.
rows: Dedicated business advisors, not an attorney
Annual tax filings prepped and filed for you
record.who: New LLC formation buyers on the middle and top plans; the page does not say how existing subscribers are treated.
record.read: Upfront prices are held while attorney access, the costly part of the service, is reserved for the top plan. That pushes customers who want legal help toward the higher tier and its higher renewal price.
record.caveat: The comparison snapshot is from 24 Oct. The phone number and some marketing copy also changed. State filing fees are extra on all plans.

items.why: Pro meetings allowance changed from Higher limits to Unlimited (subject to abuse limits), while the Free word limit no longer shows its 2,000/week figure.

record.short: Pro meetings go from Higher limits to Unlimited, and the Free word limit no longer shows 2,000/week.
record.headline: Wispr Flow now lists Notetaker meetings as unlimited on Pro and no longer states the 2,000 words a week cap on the Free plan.
record.who: Pro subscribers (looser meetings) and Free users (word cap no longer quantified).
record.read: Removing the unlimited-meeting ceiling is a perk for paying users. Hiding the Free word number may signal the cap is being adjusted, so Free users may not know their allowance.
record.caveat: Pro unlimited is marked as subject to abuse limits. The FAQ on the same page still mentions higher meeting limits, so the cap may not have changed. The Free cap may be unchanged and just no longer displayed.
